What Is Dropbox Inc?

Dropbox is a cloud-based data storage, file sharing, and work collaboration platform. The Dropbox Inc Company was started in 2007 by two students from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology as a startup company. The company has traveled its successful journey from just a $5 million company in 2007 to over a $10 billion company in 2014. Presently, the company is headquartered in San Francisco, California, USA. The company has more than 500 million registered users and over 11 million paid users. The company has 12 offices in the USA and abroad staffing over 1858 employees. It is interesting to note that the former US Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice is a director of the board of the company’s directors. The company is planning an IPO to raise $720 million this year. The services of Dropbox are widely used by businesses worldwide, including VDR providers and many more.

Top 5 Dropbox Integrations Done by Major Companies

Dropbox is already in partnership with many big companies to integrate Dropbox in their services, and working with others to take them on board. The top 5 Dropbox integrations are mentioned below:

1# Dropbox MS Office 365 Integration

Dropbox integrated with the Microsoft office 365 improves team collaboration, communication, and document sharing tremendously. This integration offers extended mobility and device compatibility. A Dropbox Android developer can use the Dropbox business integration to achieve high efficiency in the productivity and improved collaboration within a multi-discipline team.

#2 Dropbox Integration with Adobe Cloud

The business integration of Dropbox with the Adobe Document Cloud brings a simple way to edit, store, share and even handwrite the documents for the further process from anywhere in the world. You can also use any kinds of devices to work with the PDF documents. The adobe documents can directly be opened and edited from the Dropbox platform without any issues. So, you get a full freedom and smoothness in working with PDF files from the Dropbox platform.

#3 Dropbox & Slack Integration

This integration brings a secure, reliable and efficient collaborative environment powered by effective communication in a team environment. You can create new content, edit the existing content, sharing the comments, and receiving the guidelines for greater team productivity easily. This integration makes your collaboration and communication fully smooth irrespective of devices, platforms, and geographical locations.

#4 Dropbox & Salesforce Integration

The Dropbox integration with the Salesforce will improve the effectiveness of the digital marketing, eCommerce services, and sales strategies. The improvement in major marketing strategies can be achieved through effective collaboration and file sharing.

#5 Dropbox & Nintex Integration

The Nintex cloud workflow gets tremendously improved by the Dropbox integration. This integration allows efficient workflow updates, sharing, and storing the document in the real-time environment. This integration is very useful for the efficient management of company workflow.

Top 5 Alternatives of Dropbox Integrations on Websites

Hundreds of cloud storage and document management services are available in the marketplace that offers similar types of services with some differences in their features. Let’s have a look at the top 5 alternatives of Dropbox cloud storage.

#1 Google Drive

Google Cloud offers file storage, editing and sharing services. It is one of the powerful competitors of the Dropbox service.

#2 Microsoft OneDrive

Powered by the Microsoft Corporation, this service is a good alternative to Dropbox cloud storage services.

#3 Box Cloud Storage

The Box cloud storage is considered as the closest competitor of Dropbox in terms of many features and capabilities.

#4 Amazon Drive

This service is powered by the cloud giant Amazon Web Services. It offers stiff competition to the Dropbox services.

#5 pCloud Storage

It is a new service, but growing very fast. It has developed a good reputation in the marketplace.

What Questions to Ask for Hiring a Dropbox Programmer?

In a Dropbox web developer interview, the following questions should be asked to make sure that the web developer is a good fit for your project.

Q #1: What are the major SDKs supported for Dropbox app development?

Answer: SwiftyDropbox, Objective-C, Dropbox for Python, Dropbox.Net, Java SDK, Dropbox for JavaScript, and Dropbox for HTTP are officially supported SDKs. There many other community SDKs also available.

Q #2: What the projects have you done relating to the Dropbox app development?

Answer: Android Apps for photo sharing, chatting backups, eCommerce apps, online document editing event recording and many others.

Q #3: How DBX works for the application development?

Answer: You need to register with the Dropbox service. Then add your application name by using the DBX wizard. Choose either Dropbox API or Dropbox business API. Set the “App folder” and then you get an application key. Add your application directly in the folder and push for publication.

Q #4: What are the major steps for a smooth Dropbox integration?

Answer: The steps for the integration of app on DBX include registration, app development, choose permissions, add server and URL names and publish.

Q #5: How web development can benefit from DBX platform?

Answer: The Dropbox DBX platform offers full flexibility through the APIs to create web apps, mobile apps and other plugins. This improves the efficiency, productivity and effectiveness of the application.

Dropbox Web Developer Salary

The Dropbox web developer salary depends on the skill set, experience, and qualification of a developer. The average cost of a Dropbox web developer varies in different countries across the world. The average salary in the USA is about $97,453 per annum. But, the average salary of a Dropbox developer in Ukraine is about $24,652 per annum.

This proportion of the cost is also maintained in all other IT industries. That is why Eastern Europe is becoming an attractive destination not only for android development outsourcing, but also for any IT services outsourcing.
